## How the partition was chosen (from `--facts` item counts)

- **Forced limit, reported explicitly:** special-topics-in-representation-theory has exactly 3 batches and fills the 3-batch cap, so one Alpha necessarily owns 68 items — the run's largest total, not rebalanceable by Step 2.
- **Balance:** I enumerated every legal split of the other twelve batches (all block sizes ≤3, all lane counts). Subject to max ≤ 68, no partition lifts every lane to 58; five non-special lanes is forced (four lanes force a 76+ lane; six lanes drop the floor to 47). Hence band **57–68, spread 11 is optimal**, not an avoidable imbalance.
- **Crossings next:** of the 30 partitions attaining 57–68, the minimum crossing weight is **29** (verified twice with independent enumerations); picking the 57-minimum variant also keeps 3 of the 4 heaviest edges internal and has the better second-largest lane (65 vs 68).
- **Coherence tradeoff:** the price is two mixed-category lanes (a and c), acknowledged in their rationales — the same balance-over-coherence pattern used by the concluded frontier-39/40 runs. Dependency-minimal swapping was explained in each rationale (e.g. reuniting 1 with 3 would trade the 12-edge 5→3 for the 5-edge 10→9, adding 7 crossing weight).
